headline: Unanimously supported Mayor Pangallo’s stance on data centers; also approved minutes from three earlier meetings.
summary: Members discussed a state executive order on data centers and the Mayor’s statement on the issue, then voted unanimously to support the Mayor’s stance. Other updates covered a Volt & Vibe event, a Preservation in a Changing Climate conference, and a proposed native planting ordinance.
decisions: Approved minutes of June 24, 2026, July 22, 2026, and Sept. 2, 2026 Special Meeting, unanimously.
Approved a motion to support the Mayor’s stance on data centers, unanimously.

decision_evidence.quote: A motion to approve all three sets of minutes was made by Kevin Rice, seconded by Bill Burnham, and passed unanimously.
Kevin Rice motioned to support the Mayor’s stance on the issue, was seconded by Will Winn, and the motion passed unanimously.

Sustainability Dept. Updates
 Volt & Vibe recap
o Lots of Electric Unicycles were present, along with one scooter and two bikes (one of which was
a mountain bike conversion)
o Will helped with setup; John helped during the event and during breakdown
o No bike shops/vendors were able to attend. One indicated that if held on a Sunday in the

o Would be better to have bike shops there
o Stacy to connect John to Zo so he can connect him to Tony (mountain bike conversion)
 Preservation in a Changing Climate conference was a good networking opportunity and very 
informative
o Discussion of mode shift in the future would be good. Current zoning is “car centric” in most 
cases. Discovered that Newport RI is the same size as Salem
o A whole session on the Heaven and Earth Project was complemented by tours of the Church. 
They want to put the 400 geothermal wells on Salem Common
98 WASHINGTON STREET, SALEM, MASSACHUSETTS 01970 ♦ TEL: 978.745.9595 FAX: 978.740.0404 ♦  WWW.SALEMMA.GOV
 Some people may object to this if they don’t understand how geothermal wells work;  
the temporary nature of the impact and reassurances that the Common will be restored 
exactly as before should be emphasized in public engagement moving forward 
o 21 interested property owners want to be connected to the networked geothermal
o Rev. Ives is probably the best person to bring people together on this
o There is an Agent Manager because the Project will be co-owned by Church and others

o Now contributing to SRD monthly newsletter
o Launched an Instagram. Please follow salem_serc

 Kudos on Kevin’s trip to Mack Park – clips with audio
o Question to discuss: Current events and policies, how do we decide between meetings

 Stacy suggests limiting discussion between meetings to talks between

o John suggests adding SERC member (after Bonnie’s talk) discussion of Mayor’s statement 
regarding data centers to the October agenda. A SERC member should be able to 
summarize the Mayor’s stance and can post about it
 Plug-In Solar (Bill Burns and John Hayes)
o Met a week ago, discussed ideas for a future presentation
o Plan is to present facts found for discussion of MA bill coming up
o Takeaways so far:
 Legislation being considered, many other states have passed;
 Usually new state regulations limit consumer rights, but this does the opposite; 
some states have delayed as they wait for a consensus on electrical guidance and 
certification from Underwriters Lab;
 Purpose is to allow residents to buy plug-in solar without undergoing the same 
process as for rooftop solar; this bill would eliminate certain steps up to a certain 
wattage 
 Language Access (Will Winn)
o Nothing happening right now
o Some would love access in Spanish, but SERC has no resources, or it must go through the 
City;
o Subcommittee can probably be dissolved until something happens
o A meeting was held by the City for newer Committee members (of all Boards, Commissions, 
and Committees) and potential candidates. A Spanish interpreter was provided and 
speakers of languages other than English were invited. 
 Native Plantings (Kevin Rice)
o Trying to put together a presentation for all of SERC, opportunities and next steps before 
approaching City Councilors
o MA has good models, especially in Somerville, of native planting ordinances. Somerville’s 
ordinance:
  “…establishes minimum requirements for native plants and trees to be planted in 
City-owned parks, open spaces, and streets. The legislation… applies to new 
plantings carried out by the City or on behalf of the City.
 The Ordinance defines native plants and trees as those with origins in North America
east of the Mississippi River. It requires that native species constitute 100% of all 
new plantings in any City-owned land on the Community Path, the Green Line 
Extension corridor, and riverfront areas; at least 75% of new plantings in City-owned 
parks; and at least 50% of street trees and new plantings in bioswales, plazas, 
streetscapes, and other City-owned property, subject to certain exemptions.”
